name: mini_chatgpt_general_v1
description: Fixed general-language evaluation suite for M4+ base and post-trained models. Every item was written by hand for this project; none is copied from a public benchmark. Frozen: items are never edited after a model has been scored on them. A change makes a new version.

scoring.multiple_choice: Each choice is scored as the sum of log-probabilities of its tokens given the prompt. 'acc' takes the argmax of the sum; 'acc_norm' (primary) takes the argmax of the sum divided by the choice's UTF-8 byte length, so choices of different lengths and tokenizers are compared fairly. Chance = mean of 1/len(choices).
scoring.minimal_pairs: The full sentence log-probability of 'good' must exceed that of 'bad'. Chance = 0.5.
scoring.code_generation: Greedy decoding of up to 16 new tokens; correct if the decoded continuation starts with any string in 'accept'.
scoring.generation: Sampled continuations (temperature 0.7, top-k 40, 3 fixed seeds, 200 new tokens) are scored by automatic surface metrics (repetition, distinct-n, end-of-text behaviour, replacement characters) and later by a blind human rubric. No automatic judge is treated as ground truth.
scoring.chat: Instruction-following section. Applies only to models with chat special tokens after post-training. For base models only the format checks are reported, and they are expected to fail.

lm_heldout.description: Bits per UTF-8 byte on held-out documents of each domain (tokenizer-independent). Domains are taken from documents never used for training or tokenizer fitting: the M4.1 general validation split, a Wikipedia held-out set, and the TinyStories V2 validation split (regression check).

chat.description: Multi-turn conversations ending with a user turn. Checks: 'format' (the reply ends with <|end|> within 128 tokens and does not start a new <|user|> or <|assistant|> turn), 'include_any' (case-insensitive substring), 'max_sentences'. Meaningful only after post-training; base models are expected to fail.
